title: Accurate token splitting and reconciliation for streamed response chunks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We observed recurring discrepancies between the token counts reported by the client-side SDK and the billing ledger for streamed responses. The mismatch appears primarily when responses are delivered as multiple stream chunks and when clients reconnect mid-stream. Root causes likely include inconsistent tokenization versions between components, chunk boundary detokenization differences, and at-least-once stream delivery producing duplicate accounting events. This ticket scopes a deterministic, server-authoritative token delta model, durable event capture for every stream chunk, and a reconciliation pipeline that prevents double-billing and fixes historic gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Server is authoritative: every streamed chunk includes a signed token_delta and chunk_offset; token accounting computed solely from persisted events
Reconnects and at-least-once delivery do not result in >0.1% token-count discrepancy for 99th percentile of customer workloads compared to golden reference
Shadow deployment shows no increase in p99 tail latency >5% and no throughput regression for Dedicated clusters
Backfill job can reconcile prior 30 days of stream events and identify any billing gaps; must generate an audit report and suggested corrections
New dashboards with per-session token deltas, duplicate-event counts, and reconciliation drift are available in Console (metering-ops dashboard)
End-to-end tests (unit, integration, property-based) added and run in CI gating the change
technical_notes: Observed patterns: 1) Client SDK estimates tokens using tokenizer v2 while runtime uses v3 byte-pair rules -> off-by-fraction. 2) Stream chunk boundaries can split multi-byte unicode sequences and BPE tokens; naive detokenization on chunk-level undercounts or duplicates leading/trailing tokens. 3) Streaming transport retries (gRPC/HTTP) can replay chunks; existing dedup relies on ephemeral session state that is lost across reconnects. 4) Function-call structured output contains JSON string escaping that changes effective tokenization if tokenization is applied before vs after string unescaping.
implementation_plan: Add authoritative tokenization: include tokenizer_version and token_checksum fields in request metadata; runtime will compute tokenized sequence using deterministic library (same binary used for billing)
Augment streaming payload schema: each stream event will include chunk_token_delta (int) and chunk_token_offset (int) and event_seq (monotonic per session)
Persist every stream event to append-only metering table with session_id, event_seq, token_delta, token_offset, produced_by (node-id), and request_hash
Implement idempotency on ingestion: use session_id + event_seq + request_hash to detect duplicates across reconnects and de-dupe before writing billing ledger entries
Implement chunking-aware tokenizer at the runtime layer that avoids splitting within BPE token boundaries and emits 'partial_token' markers when unavoidable; partial tokens are resolved by next chunk
Add reconciliation worker: compares persisted events to daily billing ledger, computes required corrections, and emits adjustment invoices in staging for review
Coordinate with SDK teams to add session_id propagation and token_checksum generation so clients can surface parity checks to devs
test_plan: Unit tests for tokenizer parity across versions and for chunk boundary semantics (UTF-8, grapheme clusters, BPE)
Property-based fuzz tests that generate random split points in middle of multi-codepoint sequences and assert deterministic total token count after reassembly
Integration tests that simulate reconnects with event replays and assert de-duplication and correct ledger entries
End-to-end shadow run for 48h on a subset of traffic routing to new ingestion pipeline; compare shadow token totals vs current production accounting
Load test on Dedicated clusters to validate persistence throughput and p99 latency impact
Backfill dry-run on historical 30-day event log to validate reconciliation worker correctness
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy streaming payload schema changes to canary region; route 1% of traffic with shadow write-only mode (persist events but do not affect billing)
Phase 2 (validation): Run 48h shadow comparison; create reconciliation report and resolve mismatches with manual review
Phase 3 (opt-in): Enable new accounting for beta customers and Dedicated tenants who opt in; monitor metrics and customer feedback
Phase 4 (global): Flip default for all hosted traffic; run automated backfill for past 30 days; publish audit report and corrective invoices if required
Rollback criteria: >0.5% sustained drift in token totals, >5% p99 latency regression, or critical persistence errors
monitoring_and_alerting: token_checksum_mismatch_rate > 0.05% => Dev platform ticket and SDK compatibility alert
dependencies: ENG-7802: persistence-layer schema change for append-only metering table
PM-198: billing ledger adjustment support for correction invoices
